# Raman analysis of 2D and layered materials

You read the spectrum; the tools measure. Every number you report comes from a tool output (measured), a
relation applied inside its validity range (inferred, with the relation's source), or a reference entry
(literature, with its source and locator). If none applies, say so under limits.

## Start here: run these commands first (from the folder that holds the data)

Use the validated scripts below; do not write your own baseline, peak-finding or fitting code unless a script
fails or you need a check it does not provide. The scripts and notes are in `C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis`.

```
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl_qc.py" <file>                  # artifacts, Si calibration, resolution
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl_fit.py" <file> --substrate "<substrate>"   # peaks with errors + fit.png
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl_series.py" <f1> <f2> ... --labels <l1> <l2> ... --substrate "<substrate>" --si-correct   # several spectra
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl.py" match_library --positions_cm1 <p1> <p2> ... --intensities <h1> <h2> ... --x_range_cm1 <lo> <hi>
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl.py" lookup_reference_modes --material <name>
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl.py" classify_polarization --path <angle-series file>
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl.py" list_relations --material <name>
python "C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/scripts/rl.py" apply_relation --name <relation> --inputs '{"<input>": <value>}'
```
Then read `C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/reference/materials/<material>.md` (when the material is known or once you have a
candidate) and `C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/reference/artifacts.md`. Always return ranked candidates for an identify task,
even when uncertain: put the uncertainty in the confidence values and the limits, never return an empty list.

## What each script does

- `scripts/rl_qc.py <file>`: quality and condition flags (spikes, saturation, background, Si calibration offset,
  low-wavenumber cutoff, sampling, signal to noise).
- `scripts/rl_fit.py <file> [--substrate SiO2/Si] [--window LO HI] [--min-snr N]`: fitted peak table with
  uncertainties, `peaks.json`, and `fit.png` (data, baseline, components, residual). Look at the plot.
- `scripts/rl_series.py <file1> <file2> ... --labels ... [--substrate SiO2/Si] [--si-correct]`: fits every
  spectrum the same way, tracks each band across spectra (position, width, relative height, shift vs the first
  spectrum with error), separations of the two strongest bands, Si offsets, and `series.png`. Use it whenever
  there is more than one spectrum. Its errors are fit statistics only; add the calibration uncertainty (Si offset
  scatter, typically a few tenths of a cm-1) before calling a shift significant.
- `scripts/rl.py <tool> --help`: `fit_peaks`, `match_library`, `classify_polarization`,
  `lookup_reference_modes`, `list_relations`, `apply_relation`, `load_spectrum`. Outputs carry provenance.

## Workflow

0. **Read the material's literature note first** when the material is known: `C:/Users/sadit/Desktop/P_Projects/Hackathons/OSI Hackathon/skill/ramanlens/skills/raman-analysis/reference/materials/<name>.md`
   (MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2, graphene, hBN, black-phosphorus, CrSBr, CrI3-CrBr3, MPS3) plus
   `reference/materials/general-measurement.md` and, for magnets, `magnetic-raman-general.md`. They hold how the
   spectrum changes with thickness, strain, doping, defects, temperature, laser and substrate, the quality
   indicators, the known pitfalls and the questions to ask, each with its source. Interpretation without them is
   guesswork from memory.
1. **Conditions first.** Note laser wavelength, temperature, substrate, polarization geometry, resolution. Many
   conclusions depend on them (`reference/measurement-questions.md`). With a user present, ask for what is missing
   and say why it matters; otherwise state the assumption under limits.
2. **Quality check.** `rl_qc.py`. Spikes are artifacts, never peaks (`reference/artifacts.md`).
3. **Fit.** `rl_fit.py`, then look at `fit.png`. Check weak shoulders and close doublets (2LA(M) next to E2g in
   WS2); refit a window with `--window` when the residual shows structure. Report fitted positions and widths.
4. **Identify.** `rl.py match_library --positions_cm1 ... --intensities ... --x_range_cm1 LO HI` ranks
   candidates from the Computational Raman Database (DFT, frequencies typically 0 to 3 % low, fitted scale per
   candidate) and curated literature tables. Do not stop at the top score: check that the strong predicted modes
   are present and the missing ones are explainable (outside the window, selection rules, resonance). The
   matcher's irreps and space group are the best source for mode labels of uncommon materials. For a stated
   material ("verify"), compare against its reference modes; a wrong hint is common, so say inconsistent when
   strong modes are missing or extra strong bands are unexplained.
5. **Assign.** Each sample peak gets a mode label and irrep with its source: `rl.py lookup_reference_modes
   --material X` for the curated materials (graphene, 2H-MoS2, 2H-WS2, 2H-MoSe2, 2H-WSe2, CrSBr, hBN, black
   phosphorus), the matcher's CRD entry otherwise. Use the irreps of the structure you identified (bulk D6h
   labels for bulk 2H crystals, C3v A1/E for 3R, D3h for a monolayer). Assign Si lines as 'Si substrate'.
6. **Polarization** (angle series only). `rl.py classify_polarization --path <file>` classifies each band
   (isotropic_par_only, isotropic_both, twofold, fourfold, silent). Report the tool's class; use it to check
   irreps (A modes isotropic_par_only and E modes isotropic_both in uniaxial crystals; twofold in in-plane
   anisotropic crystals).
7. **Properties.** Read `reference/relations.md` and `reference/materials.md`, then `rl.py apply_relation`. Report
   layer number, strain, doping or defect density only from a relation (with its source and validity) or a
   stated rule from the notes. Name properties `layers`, `defect_level`, `L_D_nm`, `strain_sign`,
   `doping_type`, `phase` where they apply.
8. **Literature** (when the Valency and iopic-bond tools are available). Form the hypothesis first; never search by
   peak positions. See `reference/literature.md`: find the paper, view its reference spectrum figure, compare.
9. **Interpret changes** (several spectra, or a known material). Run `rl_series.py`; then for each change ask
   which mechanisms in the material note produce it (thickness, strain, doping, defects, heating, calibration,
   resonance) and which observable separates them (e.g. a rigid shift of all lines including Si is calibration;
   A1g-only shift in MoS2 points to doping, E2g shift with splitting to strain; graphene G broadening separates
   stage 1 from stage 2 defects). State the most likely reading, the alternatives, and the measurement that would
   decide between them.
10. **Report.** Ranked candidates with evidence, peaks with provenance and source, properties with relation and
   source, artifacts, citations (only sources you used), and limits: what the data cannot tell, rejected
   hypotheses, relations that did not apply and why.

## Expert habits

- One spectrum rarely fixes layer number alone; name the observable and its threshold.
- Laser heating, strain and doping shift lines by similar amounts; check calibration before reading 1 to 2 cm-1.
- Intensity ratios depend on substrate interference and laser energy; absolute intensity is not layer number.
- Resonant excitation changes relative intensities and activates second-order bands; check the laser against the
  material's excitons before calling a band unexpected.
- When something looks odd, say what it looks like and what would distinguish the explanations.

# WS2: expert Raman notes

Scope: 2H-WS2. Numbers appear only where they were read in the cited source; the locator says where.
"Consensus" means several independent sources agree; "single source" means one paper. The defining practical
issue for WS2 is the 2LA(M) overtone sitting a few cm-1 below E2g1: almost every misreading starts there.

## Signature and irreps
- Bulk D6h zone-centre modes A1g + 2A2u + 2B2g + B1u + E1g + 2E1u + 2E2g + E2u; A1g, E1g, E2g Raman active,
  E1g forbidden in backscattering (Hait S. et al. 2022, J. Appl. Phys. 132, 133901, doi:10.1063/5.0107655,
  p.4). 1L is D3h (E2g1 to E', A1g to A1'), odd N D3h, even N D3d (Yang J. et al. 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, p.5).
- At 514.5 nm, 1L: 2LA(M) 351.1, E2g1 355.2, A1g 417.2 cm-1; bulk 350.0, 355.3, 420.1; LA(M) near 176 at 488 nm
  (Berkdemir A. et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1).
- Resonant 1L spectrum also contains bands at 176, 193, 231, 353 (2LA), 583 and 702 (4LA) cm-1, all zone-edge
  combinations (Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.14, Fig. 11c, Table III).

## Thickness
- A1g stiffens with N (417.2, 418.4, 419.0, 420.1 cm-1 for 1L, 2L, 3L, bulk at 514.5 nm) while E2g1 barely moves
  (Berkdemir 2013, Table 1). Consensus on the trend. So the A1g-E2g1 separation grows only a few cm-1.
- The A1g-E2g1 separation: about 62 cm-1 in 1L to 66 in bulk, as relayed by Mitioglu A. A. et al. 2014,
  PRB 89, 245442, arXiv:1406.3511, p.2.
- 1L flags at resonance: 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio about 2 at 514 nm, decreasing with N (Berkdemir 2013).
  The ratio depends on polarization (see below), so use it only with known polarization.
- A peak near 310 cm-1 is present in multilayers and absent in 1L (Zhao W. et al. 2013, Nanoscale 5, 9677,
  arXiv:1304.0911, p.10, Fig. 5b). Assignment unclear in that paper (proposed shear-related combination).
- Low-frequency shear and breathing series determine N (Yang 2017, abstract). At A-exciton resonance the
  Raman-forbidden lowest shear mode of odd N appears as strong as the allowed even-N one, with a Fano line shape
  (Yang 2017, abstract): do not use its presence as a parity test at that laser.

## Strain and doping
- Uniaxial strain on 1L WS2 redshifts the modes, in-plane modes faster, and splits E'; WS2 shows much larger
  changes in mode positions and intensities than WSe2 under the same strain; at large strain the polarization
  response of a mode changes (Dadgar A. M. et al. 2018, Chem. Mater., doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b01672,
  arXiv:1705.05412, abstract; WS2 data Fig. 3b, calculated shifts Fig. 4c,d). Strain rates for WS2 not extracted here.
- Doping: no WS2-specific Raman doping rate verified. By analogy with MoS2 (Chakraborty 2012, see MoS2.md) an
  A1g shift with broadening would point to electron doping; this is an inference, not a WS2 measurement.

## Defects and quality
- No WS2-specific defect calibration verified. LA(M) near 176 cm-1 is present already in pristine spectra near
  resonance (Berkdemir 2013, 488 nm), so its presence alone is not a defect marker in WS2, unlike LA(M) in
  off-resonant MoS2 (inference from the two sources).
- The band near 297 cm-1 is the backscattering-forbidden E1g, and the one near 325 cm-1 is E2g2+LA (Kumar D. et al.
  2019, J. Phys. Condens. Matter, doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, arXiv:1906.10661, abstract). Hait 2022 (p.4)
  instead assigns about 325 cm-1 to an out-of-plane acoustic mode at M. Disputed.
- Phase: 1T and 1T' monolayer WS2 give different spectra and temperature behaviour (Kumar 2019, abstract).

## Temperature and heating
- Supported 1L WS2: temperature evolution of first-order and combination modes is anomalous, attributed to
  detuning of the resonance and to strain from substrate thermal-expansion mismatch; some combination modes
  disappear (Kumar 2019, abstract). Nonlinear shifts in supported WS2 were also noted by Taube A. et al. 2014,
  ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, p.5.
- Consequence: temperature changes intensities (resonance) as well as positions; a laser-heating estimate from
  peak positions needs a coefficient measured on the same substrate. No WS2 coefficient verified here.

## Excitation wavelength and resonance
- 2LA(M) lies about 4 to 5 cm-1 below E2g1 and becomes stronger than the main peaks for 1.96, 2.33 and 2.41 eV
  (A and B exciton resonance) (Yang 2017, p.5; Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Consensus.
- E2g1 is enhanced near the C exciton; A1g resonates with A, B and C (Yang 2017, p.5).
- Bulk resonance spans 1.96 to 2.41 eV because of the broad B exciton (Zhang X. 2015, p.13). 633 nm is resonant
  with the A exciton of WS2 (Zhao 2013, p.9).
- Peaks X1 and X2, independent of thickness, appear near exciton resonances; X1 vanishes in cross polarization,
  X2 does not (Yang 2017, abstract). Unassigned.

## Polarization and substrate
- 2LA intensity is minimal when excitation and detection are orthogonal and exceeds E2g1 in parallel; A1g behaves
  similarly, E2g1 is isotropic (Mitioglu 2014, p.4, Fig. 3; Yang 2017, p.5). Measure in cross polarization to
  isolate E2g1 (Yang 2017, p.5). Consensus.
- Substrate interference changes absolute and relative intensities; Yang 2017 corrects for it (p.4). Substrate
  strain enters through thermal-expansion mismatch (Kumar 2019).

## Pitfalls and artifacts
- Fitting a single Lorentzian to the 2LA/E2g1 doublet misplaces E2g1 and can give a wrong layer number
  (Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Always fit both, constrained by polarization data when possible.
- Reported 1L positions differ between groups (Hait 2022, p.4: 2LA 353.98, E2g 357.97, A1g 418.23 cm-1;
  Berkdemir 2013: 351.1, 355.2, 417.2) partly from fitting model and calibration; compare to the same source.
- Intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line, polarization and substrate.

## What to ask
- Laser line (resonance changes the spectrum completely), power and spot size.
- Polarization: unpolarized, parallel or crossed; analyser present?
- Substrate and oxide thickness; CVD or exfoliated; transferred; encapsulated.
- Measurement temperature; phase (2H vs 1T or 1T') if chemically processed.
- Fit model used for the 350 cm-1 region.

## Reference figures
- Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5: 1L to 5L and bulk at 532 nm, normalized to 2LA(M); 310 cm-1 band inset.
- Mitioglu 2014, arXiv:1406.3511, Fig. 3: 2LA/E2g1 and A1g regions vs polarization angle (1L).
- Yang 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, Fig. 1c,d: thickness dependence of main and weak peaks at 2.54 eV.
- Berkdemir 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Fig. 3 (open access, not on arXiv): 1L to bulk at 514.5 nm.

# WS2: expert Raman notes

Scope: 2H-WS2. Numbers appear only where they were read in the cited source; the locator says where.
"Consensus" means several independent sources agree; "single source" means one paper. The defining practical
issue for WS2 is the 2LA(M) overtone sitting a few cm-1 below E2g1: almost every misreading starts there.

## Signature and irreps
- Bulk D6h zone-centre modes A1g + 2A2u + 2B2g + B1u + E1g + 2E1u + 2E2g + E2u; A1g, E1g, E2g Raman active,
  E1g forbidden in backscattering (Hait S. et al. 2022, J. Appl. Phys. 132, 133901, doi:10.1063/5.0107655,
  p.4). 1L is D3h (E2g1 to E', A1g to A1'), odd N D3h, even N D3d (Yang J. et al. 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, p.5).
- At 514.5 nm, 1L: 2LA(M) 351.1, E2g1 355.2, A1g 417.2 cm-1; bulk 350.0, 355.3, 420.1; LA(M) near 176 at 488 nm
  (Berkdemir A. et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1).
- Resonant 1L spectrum also contains bands at 176, 193, 231, 353 (2LA), 583 and 702 (4LA) cm-1, all zone-edge
  combinations (Zhang X. et al. 2015, Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757, arXiv:1502.00701, p.14, Fig. 11c, Table III).

## Thickness
- A1g stiffens with N (417.2, 418.4, 419.0, 420.1 cm-1 for 1L, 2L, 3L, bulk at 514.5 nm) while E2g1 barely moves
  (Berkdemir 2013, Table 1). Consensus on the trend. So the A1g-E2g1 separation grows only a few cm-1.
- The A1g-E2g1 separation: about 62 cm-1 in 1L to 66 in bulk, as relayed by Mitioglu A. A. et al. 2014,
  PRB 89, 245442, arXiv:1406.3511, p.2.
- 1L flags at resonance: 2LA(M)/A1g intensity ratio about 2 at 514 nm, decreasing with N (Berkdemir 2013).
  The ratio depends on polarization (see below), so use it only with known polarization.
- A peak near 310 cm-1 is present in multilayers and absent in 1L (Zhao W. et al. 2013, Nanoscale 5, 9677,
  arXiv:1304.0911, p.10, Fig. 5b). Assignment unclear in that paper (proposed shear-related combination).
- Low-frequency shear and breathing series determine N (Yang 2017, abstract). At A-exciton resonance the
  Raman-forbidden lowest shear mode of odd N appears as strong as the allowed even-N one, with a Fano line shape
  (Yang 2017, abstract): do not use its presence as a parity test at that laser.

## Strain and doping
- Uniaxial strain on 1L WS2 redshifts the modes, in-plane modes faster, and splits E'; WS2 shows much larger
  changes in mode positions and intensities than WSe2 under the same strain; at large strain the polarization
  response of a mode changes (Dadgar A. M. et al. 2018, Chem. Mater., doi:10.1021/acs.chemmater.8b01672,
  arXiv:1705.05412, abstract; WS2 data Fig. 3b, calculated shifts Fig. 4c,d). Strain rates for WS2 not extracted here.
- Doping: no WS2-specific Raman doping rate verified. By analogy with MoS2 (Chakraborty 2012, see MoS2.md) an
  A1g shift with broadening would point to electron doping; this is an inference, not a WS2 measurement.

## Defects and quality
- No WS2-specific defect calibration verified. LA(M) near 176 cm-1 is present already in pristine spectra near
  resonance (Berkdemir 2013, 488 nm), so its presence alone is not a defect marker in WS2, unlike LA(M) in
  off-resonant MoS2 (inference from the two sources).
- The band near 297 cm-1 is the backscattering-forbidden E1g, and the one near 325 cm-1 is E2g2+LA (Kumar D. et al.
  2019, J. Phys. Condens. Matter, doi:10.1088/1361-648X/ab3fec, arXiv:1906.10661, abstract). Hait 2022 (p.4)
  instead assigns about 325 cm-1 to an out-of-plane acoustic mode at M. Disputed.
- Phase: 1T and 1T' monolayer WS2 give different spectra and temperature behaviour (Kumar 2019, abstract).

## Temperature and heating
- Supported 1L WS2: temperature evolution of first-order and combination modes is anomalous, attributed to
  detuning of the resonance and to strain from substrate thermal-expansion mismatch; some combination modes
  disappear (Kumar 2019, abstract). Nonlinear shifts in supported WS2 were also noted by Taube A. et al. 2014,
  ACS AMI, doi:10.1021/am502359k, p.5.
- Consequence: temperature changes intensities (resonance) as well as positions; a laser-heating estimate from
  peak positions needs a coefficient measured on the same substrate. No WS2 coefficient verified here.

## Excitation wavelength and resonance
- 2LA(M) lies about 4 to 5 cm-1 below E2g1 and becomes stronger than the main peaks for 1.96, 2.33 and 2.41 eV
  (A and B exciton resonance) (Yang 2017, p.5; Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Consensus.
- E2g1 is enhanced near the C exciton; A1g resonates with A, B and C (Yang 2017, p.5).
- Bulk resonance spans 1.96 to 2.41 eV because of the broad B exciton (Zhang X. 2015, p.13). 633 nm is resonant
  with the A exciton of WS2 (Zhao 2013, p.9).
- Peaks X1 and X2, independent of thickness, appear near exciton resonances; X1 vanishes in cross polarization,
  X2 does not (Yang 2017, abstract). Unassigned.

## Polarization and substrate
- 2LA intensity is minimal when excitation and detection are orthogonal and exceeds E2g1 in parallel; A1g behaves
  similarly, E2g1 is isotropic (Mitioglu 2014, p.4, Fig. 3; Yang 2017, p.5). Measure in cross polarization to
  isolate E2g1 (Yang 2017, p.5). Consensus.
- Substrate interference changes absolute and relative intensities; Yang 2017 corrects for it (p.4). Substrate
  strain enters through thermal-expansion mismatch (Kumar 2019).

## Pitfalls and artifacts
- Fitting a single Lorentzian to the 2LA/E2g1 doublet misplaces E2g1 and can give a wrong layer number
  (Mitioglu 2014, abstract). Always fit both, constrained by polarization data when possible.
- Reported 1L positions differ between groups (Hait 2022, p.4: 2LA 353.98, E2g 357.97, A1g 418.23 cm-1;
  Berkdemir 2013: 351.1, 355.2, 417.2) partly from fitting model and calibration; compare to the same source.
- Intensity ratios are only comparable at the same laser line, polarization and substrate.

## What to ask
- Laser line (resonance changes the spectrum completely), power and spot size.
- Polarization: unpolarized, parallel or crossed; analyser present?
- Substrate and oxide thickness; CVD or exfoliated; transferred; encapsulated.
- Measurement temperature; phase (2H vs 1T or 1T') if chemically processed.
- Fit model used for the 350 cm-1 region.

## Reference figures
- Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5: 1L to 5L and bulk at 532 nm, normalized to 2LA(M); 310 cm-1 band inset.
- Mitioglu 2014, arXiv:1406.3511, Fig. 3: 2LA/E2g1 and A1g regions vs polarization angle (1L).
- Yang 2017, arXiv:1706.01677, Fig. 1c,d: thickness dependence of main and weak peaks at 2.54 eV.
- Berkdemir 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Fig. 3 (open access, not on arXiv): 1L to bulk at 514.5 nm.

input.summary: Yes, spot 1 is most likely a monolayer (1L) WS2. Spot 2 is thick, 3L or more and probably bulk. Both spectra are 2H-WS2 excited near the A/B excitons at 514.5 nm: a 2LA(M)+E2g¹ doublet at about 351/355 cm⁻¹, A1g at 417–420 cm⁻¹, weak LA(M) at about 175 cm⁻¹, and the Si line at 520.8–520.9 cm⁻¹. Spot 1 has A1g at 417.29 cm⁻¹ and an A1g−E2g¹ separation of about 62.0 cm⁻¹. Its 2LA(M) is much stronger than A1g (area ratio about 4.4). All three match the 1L values of Berkdemir 2013. Spot 2 has A1g at 420.08 cm⁻¹, a separation of about 64.7 cm⁻¹ and 2LA/A1g of about 0.9, which match the 3L/bulk values. Caveats: the 1L call rests on three observables that agree with each other but come from one fit model and unknown polarization. The 3L-versus-bulk question for spot 2 cannot be settled from this data.

observations.finding: The default one-peak fit of the ~350 cm⁻¹ region is wrong for both spots. It merges 2LA(M) and E2g¹, which gives a single band at 351.7 (spot 1) and 353.0 (spot 2) and inflates the A1g−'E2g' separation to 65.6 and 67.0 cm⁻¹. A two-component fit is required.
observations.evidence: A single pseudo-Voigt gives unweighted redchi 707 (spot 1) and 2801 (spot 2); two components give 161 and 207. Absolute values are not meaningful (no noise weights), but the 4–14x drop and the residual structure in fit.png at ~355 cm⁻¹ show the doublet. The ALS baseline also inflates the single-peak tails. Fit window 325–385 cm⁻¹, linear baseline.
observations.source: Pitfall described in Mitioglu et al. 2014 PRB 89, 245442 (abstract) and WS2 note

observations.finding: Spot 1: 2LA(M) 351.10±0.07 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 8.9), E2g¹ 355.29±0.08 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~4), A1g 417.29±0.03 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 4.5), LA(M) 175.9±0.2 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 9.3). A1g−E2g¹ separation ≈ 62.0 cm⁻¹ and 2LA(M) is dominant.
observations.evidence: Doublet fit (325–385 cm⁻¹) plus A1g window fit (400–440 cm⁻¹); rl_fit for LA(M). 2LA(M)/A1g area ratio ≈ 4.4 (25300/5700); height ratio of the merged 352 band to A1g = 2.35. Si offset +0.21 cm⁻¹ (spot 1) is small compared with the 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g difference between spots.

observations.finding: Spot 2: 2LA(M) 349.9±0.1 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~8.9), E2g¹ 355.40±0.04 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~4.1), A1g 420.08±0.02 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 4.4), LA(M) 175.3±0.6 cm⁻¹. A1g−E2g¹ separation ≈ 64.7 cm⁻¹. 2LA(M) is weaker than A1g (area ratio ≈ 0.9).
observations.evidence: Same fit protocol as spot 1. Relation output: candidates 3L and bulk, low confidence (Berkdemir Δ: 3L 64.6, bulk 64.8). Si offset +0.08 cm⁻¹.

observations.finding: Difference between spots: A1g stiffens by 2.79 cm⁻¹ (417.29 to 420.08), 2LA(M) softens by about 1.2 cm⁻¹ (351.1 to 349.9), E2g¹ is essentially unchanged (355.29 vs 355.40, within ~0.1 cm⁻¹ statistical error), and 2LA/A1g drops from ~4.4 to ~0.9. This is the thickness signature in WS2. A1g linewidth is unchanged (4.5 vs 4.4 cm⁻¹) and 2LA(M) and E2g¹ widths are similar, so the crystal quality of the two spots appears comparable.
observations.evidence: Differences between the doublet and A1g fits. Rigid calibration shift is excluded because the Si line is within 0.13 cm⁻¹ and E2g¹ does not move. Strain or doping would not produce a 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g stiffening alongside this ratio change.

observations.finding: Literature match: the spot 1 positions equal the 1L values at 514.5 nm and the spot 2 positions equal the bulk values. Berkdemir values: 1L 2LA 351.1, E2g¹ 355.2, A1g 417.2; bulk 350.0, 355.3, 420.1 cm⁻¹. Spot 1 deviates by ≤0.1 cm⁻¹ in all three lines; spot 2 by 0.1 (E2g¹) and 0.0 (A1g) with 2LA 0.15 below. The 2LA(M)/A1g ratio of about 2 for 1L at 514 nm is the literature flag; the measured ~4.4 is stronger, which does not argue against 1L because the ratio depends on polarization and substrate.
observations.evidence: Measured values from the fits above compared with Berkdemir Table 1; rl apply_relation ws2_layer_number_from_separation: Δ=62.0 gives 1L (high confidence, candidate list 1L only, delta_err 0.3); Δ=64.7 gives 3L/bulk (low confidence).
observations.source: Berkdemir et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1 (514.5 nm)

observations.finding: Mode assignment (bulk D6h; 1L D3h): ~175 cm⁻¹ LA(M) (zone-edge, resonance-activated); ~350–351 cm⁻¹ 2LA(M) overtone (second order, not a Γ mode); ~355 cm⁻¹ E2g¹ (E′ in 1L); ~417–420 cm⁻¹ A1g (A1′ in 1L); 520.8–520.9 cm⁻¹ Si substrate. E1g (~297 cm⁻¹) is forbidden in backscattering and not seen.
observations.evidence: Positions from the fits; no peak in 295–325 cm⁻¹ above noise (max 490 vs median 452 for spot 1, std 21).
observations.source: Berkdemir 2013 Table 1; Zhang et al. 2015 Chem. Soc. Rev. 44, 2757 (Fig. 11c, Table III); Hait et al. 2022 J. Appl. Phys. 132, 133901 (p.4)

observations.finding: The strong 2LA(M) and LA(M) bands show the excitation is resonant with the A/B excitons. LA(M) near 176 cm⁻¹ is not a defect marker here, so it does not indicate a defective island.
observations.evidence: LA(M) present in both spots (area 1617 and 775) with similar FWHM (~9–10 cm⁻¹); 2LA(M) dominates spot 1.
observations.source: Berkdemir 2013 (LA(M) in pristine spectra near resonance); Yang et al. 2017 arXiv:1706.01677 p.5; WS2 note

properties.value: spot 1: 1 (monolayer), high confidence from the A1g−E2g¹ separation of 62.0 cm⁻¹ and consistent with A1g at 417.3 cm⁻¹ and 2LA/A1g; spot 2: 3L or bulk (not distinguishable), thick region
properties.source: Berkdemir et al. 2013, Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, Table 1 (via apply_relation ws2_layer_number_from_separation)

properties.value: 2H (E2g¹ and A1g with LA(M) and 2LA(M) at the expected 2H positions; 1T/1T′ not indicated)
properties.source: Kumar et al. 2019 J. Phys.: Condens. Matter, arXiv:1906.10661 (abstract); comparison with 2H values in Berkdemir 2013

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: low to not resolved: narrow A1g (4.4–4.5 cm⁻¹), same in both spots; no WS2-specific defect calibration exists

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: none resolved (E2g¹ at 355.3 vs 355.2 literature, within error)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: not determined (no verified WS2 doping rate; A1g position is explained by thickness)

caveats: The A1g−E2g¹ separation depends on how the doublet is fitted. E2g¹ is a weak shoulder (area ~10% of 2LA in spot 1) and the fit assumes Lorentzian/pseudo-Voigt shapes. Fits were done without noise weights, so redchi values are only relative. I adopted ±0.3 cm⁻¹ on Δ; its nearest alternative is 2L at 63.4 cm⁻¹, ~1.4 cm⁻¹ away, so 1L is favoured but the margin is about 4σ of the adopted error.

Strongest argument for 1L is that three independent observables agree (Δ, A1g position, 2LA/A1g dominance), plus a quiet region near 310 cm⁻¹. However, the 310 cm⁻¹ multilayer band (Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5b) is not resolved even in spot 2 at the present noise, so its absence in spot 1 carries no weight.

Intensity ratios depend on polarization, substrate oxide thickness and laser energy; the 2LA/A1g ratio (≈4.4 vs the literature ≈2) cannot be used quantitatively without knowing polarization and SiO2 thickness.

Calibration: Si offsets are +0.21 (spot 1) and +0.08 cm⁻¹ (spot 2), so a rigid shift cannot explain the 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g change. Si line is much weaker in spot 2 (height ~117 vs 1234) because the thick flake absorbs the beam and Si signal, consistent with a thick flake and a thin island. The Si-intensity drop is not by itself proof of thickness.

Spot 1 values equal Berkdemir 1L to ≤0.1 cm⁻¹, which is unusually good; reported 1L positions differ between groups by 1–3 cm⁻¹ (Hait 2022: 353.98/357.97/418.23) because of fit model and calibration, so the comparison is only valid against the same reference (Berkdemir).

A1g position in CVD WS2 can also be shifted by doping and by substrate-induced strain or by a few-layer island that is not uniform; a spot-size average over a 1L/2L boundary or a small bilayer nucleus at the island centre would give an intermediate separation. The data are one point per island.

Data stop at 120 cm⁻¹, so the low-frequency shear/breathing modes, the most reliable layer-number counters, are not observable; absence is not evidence. At the A-exciton resonance the shear mode is also not a valid parity test (Yang 2017).
Laser heating/power not known; supported 1L WS2 shows anomalous temperature and resonance behaviour (Kumar 2019), and heating could soften all lines.

caveats: The A1g−E2g¹ separation depends on how the doublet is fitted. E2g¹ is a weak shoulder (area ~10% of 2LA in spot 1) and the fit assumes Lorentzian/pseudo-Voigt shapes. Fits were done without noise weights, so redchi values are only relative. I adopted ±0.3 cm⁻¹ on Δ; its nearest alternative is 2L at 63.4 cm⁻¹, ~1.4 cm⁻¹ away, so 1L is favoured but the margin is about 4σ of the adopted error.

Strongest argument for 1L is that three independent observables agree (Δ, A1g position, 2LA/A1g dominance), plus a quiet region near 310 cm⁻¹. However, the 310 cm⁻¹ multilayer band (Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5b) is not resolved even in spot 2 at the present noise, so its absence in spot 1 carries no weight.

Intensity ratios depend on polarization, substrate oxide thickness and laser energy; the 2LA/A1g ratio (≈4.4 vs the literature ≈2) cannot be used quantitatively without knowing polarization and SiO2 thickness.

Calibration: Si offsets are +0.21 (spot 1) and +0.08 cm⁻¹ (spot 2), so a rigid shift cannot explain the 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g change. Si line is much weaker in spot 2 (height ~117 vs 1234) because the thick flake absorbs the beam and Si signal, consistent with a thick flake and a thin island. structured_output.summary: Yes, spot 1 is most likely a monolayer (1L) WS2. Spot 2 is thick, 3L or more and probably bulk. Both spectra are 2H-WS2 excited near the A/B excitons at 514.5 nm: a 2LA(M)+E2g¹ doublet at about 351/355 cm⁻¹, A1g at 417–420 cm⁻¹, weak LA(M) at about 175 cm⁻¹, and the Si line at 520.8–520.9 cm⁻¹. Spot 1 has A1g at 417.29 cm⁻¹ and an A1g−E2g¹ separation of about 62.0 cm⁻¹. Its 2LA(M) is much stronger than A1g (area ratio about 4.4). All three match the 1L values of Berkdemir 2013. Spot 2 has A1g at 420.08 cm⁻¹, a separation of about 64.7 cm⁻¹ and 2LA/A1g of about 0.9, which match the 3L/bulk values. Caveats: the 1L call rests on three observables that agree with each other but come from one fit model and unknown polarization. The 3L-versus-bulk question for spot 2 cannot be settled from this data.

observations.finding: The default one-peak fit of the ~350 cm⁻¹ region is wrong for both spots. It merges 2LA(M) and E2g¹, which gives a single band at 351.7 (spot 1) and 353.0 (spot 2) and inflates the A1g−'E2g' separation to 65.6 and 67.0 cm⁻¹. A two-component fit is required.
observations.evidence: A single pseudo-Voigt gives unweighted redchi 707 (spot 1) and 2801 (spot 2); two components give 161 and 207. Absolute values are not meaningful (no noise weights), but the 4–14x drop and the residual structure in fit.png at ~355 cm⁻¹ show the doublet. The ALS baseline also inflates the single-peak tails. Fit window 325–385 cm⁻¹, linear baseline.
observations.source: Pitfall described in Mitioglu et al. 2014 PRB 89, 245442 (abstract) and WS2 note

observations.finding: Spot 1: 2LA(M) 351.10±0.07 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 8.9), E2g¹ 355.29±0.08 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~4), A1g 417.29±0.03 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 4.5), LA(M) 175.9±0.2 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 9.3). A1g−E2g¹ separation ≈ 62.0 cm⁻¹ and 2LA(M) is dominant.
observations.evidence: Doublet fit (325–385 cm⁻¹) plus A1g window fit (400–440 cm⁻¹); rl_fit for LA(M). 2LA(M)/A1g area ratio ≈ 4.4 (25300/5700); height ratio of the merged 352 band to A1g = 2.35. Si offset +0.21 cm⁻¹ (spot 1) is small compared with the 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g difference between spots.

observations.finding: Spot 2: 2LA(M) 349.9±0.1 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~8.9), E2g¹ 355.40±0.04 cm⁻¹ (FWHM ~4.1), A1g 420.08±0.02 cm⁻¹ (FWHM 4.4), LA(M) 175.3±0.6 cm⁻¹. A1g−E2g¹ separation ≈ 64.7 cm⁻¹. 2LA(M) is weaker than A1g (area ratio ≈ 0.9).
observations.evidence: Same fit protocol as spot 1. Relation output: candidates 3L and bulk, low confidence (Berkdemir Δ: 3L 64.6, bulk 64.8). Si offset +0.08 cm⁻¹.

observations.finding: Difference between spots: A1g stiffens by 2.79 cm⁻¹ (417.29 to 420.08), 2LA(M) softens by about 1.2 cm⁻¹ (351.1 to 349.9), E2g¹ is essentially unchanged (355.29 vs 355.40, within ~0.1 cm⁻¹ statistical error), and 2LA/A1g drops from ~4.4 to ~0.9. This is the thickness signature in WS2. A1g linewidth is unchanged (4.5 vs 4.4 cm⁻¹) and 2LA(M) and E2g¹ widths are similar, so the crystal quality of the two spots appears comparable.
observations.evidence: Differences between the doublet and A1g fits. Rigid calibration shift is excluded because the Si line is within 0.13 cm⁻¹ and E2g¹ does not move. Strain or doping would not produce a 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g stiffening alongside this ratio change.

observations.finding: Literature match: the spot 1 positions equal the 1L values at 514.5 nm and the spot 2 positions equal the bulk values. Berkdemir values: 1L 2LA 351.1, E2g¹ 355.2, A1g 417.2; bulk 350.0, 355.3, 420.1 cm⁻¹. Spot 1 deviates by ≤0.1 cm⁻¹ in all three lines; spot 2 by 0.1 (E2g¹) and 0.0 (A1g) with 2LA 0.15 below. The 2LA(M)/A1g ratio of about 2 for 1L at 514 nm is the literature flag; the measured ~4.4 is stronger, which does not argue against 1L because the ratio depends on polarization and substrate.

caveats: The A1g−E2g¹ separation depends on how the doublet is fitted. E2g¹ is a weak shoulder (area ~10% of 2LA in spot 1) and the fit assumes Lorentzian/pseudo-Voigt shapes. Fits were done without noise weights, so redchi values are only relative. I adopted ±0.3 cm⁻¹ on Δ; its nearest alternative is 2L at 63.4 cm⁻¹, ~1.4 cm⁻¹ away, so 1L is favoured but the margin is about 4σ of the adopted error.

Strongest argument for 1L is that three independent observables agree (Δ, A1g position, 2LA/A1g dominance), plus a quiet region near 310 cm⁻¹. However, the 310 cm⁻¹ multilayer band (Zhao 2013, arXiv:1304.0911, Fig. 5b) is not resolved even in spot 2 at the present noise, so its absence in spot 1 carries no weight.

Intensity ratios depend on polarization, substrate oxide thickness and laser energy; the 2LA/A1g ratio (≈4.4 vs the literature ≈2) cannot be used quantitatively without knowing polarization and SiO2 thickness.

Calibration: Si offsets are +0.21 (spot 1) and +0.08 cm⁻¹ (spot 2), so a rigid shift cannot explain the 2.8 cm⁻¹ A1g change. Si line is much weaker in spot 2 (height ~117 vs 1234) because the thick flake absorbs the beam and Si signal, consistent with a thick flake and a thin island. The Si-intensity drop is not by itself proof of thickness.

Spot 1 values equal Berkdemir 1L to ≤0.1 cm⁻¹, which is unusually good; reported 1L positions differ between groups by 1–3 cm⁻¹ (Hait 2022: 353.98/357.97/418.23) because of fit model and calibration, so the comparison is only valid against the same reference (Berkdemir).

A1g position in CVD WS2 can also be shifted by doping and by substrate-induced strain or by a few-layer island that is not uniform; a spot-size average over a 1L/2L boundary or a small bilayer nucleus at the island centre would give an intermediate separation. The data are one point per island.

Data stop at 120 cm⁻¹, so the low-frequency shear/breathing modes, the most reliable layer-number counters, are not observable; absence is not evidence. At the A-exciton resonance the shear mode is also not a valid parity test (Yang 2017).
Laser heating/power not known; supported 1L WS2 shows anomalous temperature and resonance behaviour (Kumar 2019), and heating could soften all lines.
questions_for_user: Was the measurement unpolarized, or parallel/crossed polarization? The 2LA/A1g ratio depends strongly on this (Mitioglu 2014), and crossed polarization would isolate E2g¹ and tighten Δ.
What laser power and spot size were used? Needed to rule out heating or resonance detuning shifts of 1–2 cm⁻¹.
What is the SiO2 thickness? It sets the interference contrast and hence the intensity ratios and the weak Si signal on spot 2.
Do you have a PL spectrum of the island? A single A-exciton peak near 2.0 eV, strongly enhanced versus the thick spot, would confirm the monolayer independently of the Raman fit.
Can you provide data below 120 cm⁻¹ or an AFM height (monolayer WS2 ≈ 0.7–0.8 nm)? Either would settle 1L versus 2L and 3L versus bulk directly.
Is the island uniform? A Raman map of A1g position would show whether spot 1 sits at a 1L/2L boundary or on a multilayer nucleation core.

limits: Layer number comes from a single relation (A1g−E2g¹ separation) calibrated on CVD layers on SiO2/Si at 514.5 nm, applied inside its validity range (61–66 cm⁻¹); it cannot separate 3L from bulk.
No WS2-specific relations for strain, doping or defect density were available, so none of these are quantified; absence of a shift is the only statement on strain.

The data cannot say anything about the shear/breathing modes (cut off at 120 cm⁻¹), polarization/irrep behaviour (single polarization state, no angle series), temperature, or magnetic order (not relevant for 2H-WS2).
I did not search the literature databases for additional papers; the references are those in the supplied WS2 note and relations table. Berkdemir 2013 is not on arXiv, so its figures were not viewed.
Rejected hypotheses: spot 1 being 2L (Δ 1.4 cm⁻¹ from 63.4 and A1g 1 cm⁻¹ too high) and the single-peak E2g reading (it merges the 2LA(M) overtone).
